claim: On December 5, 2023, Amazon launched three new metrics on the FBA Manage Inventory Health Report.
evidence: On December 5, 2023, we launched three new metrics on the FBA Manage Inventory Health Report.

claim: The fba-minimum-inventory-level metric is meant to help FBA sellers plan inventory levels and avoid the low-inventory-level fee.
evidence: improve delivery speeds, and help them to avoid the recently announced low-inventory-level fee.

claim: The historical-days-of-supply metric lets sellers identify products that held low inventory relative to sales over the past 90 days and may incur low-inventory-level fees.
evidence: relative to sales over the past 90 days, and may incur low-inventory-level fees.

claim: The fba-inventory-level-health-status metric evaluates sellable inventory against the recommended minimum level and estimated excess units.
evidence: against the recommended minimum level and estimated excess units.

claim: Amazon says keeping inventory above the minimum recommended level helps improve delivery speeds and avoid the low-inventory-level fee.
evidence: Keeping inventory above the minimum recommended level helps sellers improve delivery speeds and avoid the recently announced low-inventory-level fee.

claim: The Manage Inventory Health report with these metrics is available for sellers and API integrators to pull via API.
evidence: The report is available for sellers and API integrators to pull via API.

claim: Amazon says the low-inventory-level fee is currently assessed using trailing 30- and 90-day sales.
evidence: Today, the fee is assessed using trailing 30- and 90-day sales.

claim: In its 2027 fee update, Amazon said that effective February 1 the low-inventory-level fee will apply only when inventory falls below 28 days of supply; that sentence gives no year (the update's storage changes are dated February 1, 2027).
evidence: Effective February 1, the fee will apply only when your inventory falls below 28 days of supply,
verifier_note: Source sentence says 'Effective February 1' with no year; page no longer states 2027 for this change. KeyFact re-pointed from claim 13 (storage surcharge) to this claim.

claim: Under the same update, the fee will be based on actual shipments in both the four weeks before and after the assessment date.
evidence: based on actual shipments in both the four weeks before and after the assessment date.
verifier_note: Removed '2027' from the date; the source gives 'February 1' without a year for this change.

claim: Amazon says evaluating sales in the four weeks after the assessment confirms whether low inventory reflects ongoing demand.
evidence: By also evaluating sales in the four weeks after the inventory assessment, this change confirms whether low inventory reflects ongoing demand.

claim: Amazon says the change will target SKUs that need replenishment and reduce instances triggered by unexpected demand spikes or end-of-season and end-of-life products.
evidence: This will target SKUs that need replenishment and reduce instances triggered by unexpected demand spikes or end-of-season and end-of-life products.

claim: Amazon describes the update as better reflecting sellers' actual demand.
evidence: We’re also updating the low-inventory-level fee to better reflect your actual demand.

claim: Amazon's 2027 storage changes, effective February 1, 2027, eliminate the storage utilization surcharge, which Amazon says makes it easier to stock up ahead of high-demand events.
evidence: Effective February 1, 2027, we’ll eliminate the storage utilization surcharge, which will make it easier to stock up ahead of high-demand events.

claim: Amazon's inventory management guide lists over 90 days of supply and at least one unit aged over 90 days among the situations in which it considers you to have excess inventory.
evidence: Amazon considers you to have excess inventory if you have: Over 90 days of supply At least one unit aged over 90 days
verifier_note: Source list also includes 'a better ROI opportunity'; claim and page reworded as 'among'.

claim: Amazon's inventory guide advises having about two months of supply available.
evidence: Ensure you have about two months of supply available

claim: Amazon says AWD auto-replenishment monitors inventory levels in Prime-ready fulfillment centers and triggers replenishments to keep products in stock.
evidence: monitors the inventory levels in Prime-ready fulfillment centers and triggers replenishments in order to maintain adequate inventory levels so that your products stay in stock

claim: For 2026, Amazon listed maintaining healthy inventory levels as one way to reach lower fee options.
evidence: including by updating your product packaging, selecting lower cost inbound shipment options, and maintaining healthy inventory levels.

claim: Amazon's FBA aged inventory charge applies monthly to all items stored in a fulfillment center for more than 181 days.
evidence: Charged monthly for all items stored in a fulfillment center for more than 181 days.

claim: Amazon's inventory guide says low stock levels can hurt your sales and brand reputation.
evidence: Low stock levels can hurt your sales and brand reputation.
